scoring.new_proper_name: A proper name a drafted fact writes that the world (at the undone copy) has no entry or other name for: a person, place, people, named event, named group or named object. A title on its own ('the Tsar'), an office or rank ('High Chancellor'), a people's adjective on its own ('Moscavian'), a date, and the entry's own names don't count. A titled person counts once ('Tsar Ivan III'). Counted by hand from the facts, with names.unknown_proper_phrases recorded per fact as a starting list.
scoring.stub_proposed: A row of the draft's new names (the 'New names' rows a ticked accept would make stubs of). Before the change there is no such list, so 0.
scoring.covered: A new proper name some proposed stub covers (by its name, one of its written forms, or its aka).
scoring.false_stub: A proposed stub that is no new proper name by the rule above (a title, an office, a description, a name the world has).
scoring.pass_hint: Not a bar (3 calls). The after run should cover most new proper names with no false stubs; a title or office row is a F5 failure.
scoring.long_tag: Ruling H9 follow-up: a proposed stub's tag of more than 2 words (split on whitespace, as stored after clean_tag). Compared between run 'after' (H8) and run 'after-h9' (with create-thing's tag rule), 3 calls each, same prompt and world; false stubs counted as above.
